phase: Actual matched-activity intervention on the two frozen endpoint networks
rationale: The prespecified 1-s pilot deficit increased, while 20-100-ms deficits decreased. Test whether network response organization differs at the same actual activity, without selecting a favorable window.
budget_definition: Total E+I spikes per second, assigning one activity-cost unit to every spike. This controls a stated activity proxy, not measured joules. Both cell types are included.
actuator: One positive multiplicative threshold gain applied equally to the original E and I thresholds. Gain is calibrated separately for each endpoint using the same calibration stimuli and noise seeds, then held fixed on independent test stimuli.
primary_response: Count across all 375 neurons, equally pooled over the fixed test bank; this matches the total-spike activity budget. E-only and I-only distributions are secondary checks.
primary_comparison: Learned endpoint minus initial endpoint entropy deficit at matched total activity. Negative differences favor proximity to the stated Gibbs response reference.
task_readout: Leaky-integrated 3D waveform reconstructed by an ordinary least-squares decoder fitted on calibration responses and scored on held-out templates. Same data preprocessing and decoder class in both states. This is a separate task check, not calibration of MI.
training_inference: Both endpoints belong to one pre-existing learned trajectory. New test templates and noise repeats are not independent training runs.
full_experiment_gate: Proceed to independent training replication only if actual budget matching is feasible and yields an interpretable effect worth testing. Report the predeclared 1-s outcome and all short-window outcomes; do not rename a selected sensitivity as the original primary outcome.
